rules.title: Ingress extensions/v1beta1 is no longer served
rules.summary: The Kubernetes Deprecated API Migration Guide states that the extensions/v1beta1 API version of Ingress is no longer served as of v1.22, which was released on 2021-08-04.

constraints: Keep routing behavior unchanged: the same hosts, paths, and backends.

In networking.k8s.io/v1, spec.backend is renamed spec.defaultBackend, and each backend's serviceName and servicePort become service.name and service.port.number (or service.port.name for a named port).
pathType is required on every path in networking.k8s.io/v1; use ImplementationSpecific to keep the old undefined behavior, or Prefix or Exact if that is what was intended.
If an Ingress is selected by an ingress class annotation, check the IngressClass resource still matches.

steps.title: Change the Ingress apiVersion
steps.instructions: Change the reported `apiVersion` to `networking.k8s.io/v1`.

steps.title: Rewrite backends and paths
steps.instructions: Rename spec.backend to spec.defaultBackend, convert serviceName and servicePort to the service.name and service.port forms, and add a pathType to every path.

steps.title: Align other Ingress declarations
steps.instructions: Update every other manifest, Helm template, and kustomize patch or target that names the old Ingress API version, so the repository agrees.

verification.purpose: Validate the migrated manifests against the schemas of the target Kubernetes version.
Ask a cluster on the target version to accept the migrated manifest without applying it.
For a Helm chart, render it and validate the output.

rules.title: PodSecurityPolicy policy/v1beta1 is no longer served
rules.summary: The Kubernetes Deprecated API Migration Guide states that the policy/v1beta1 API version of PodSecurityPolicy is no longer served as of v1.25, which was released on 2022-08-23.
rules.replacement: Pod Security Admission or a 3rd party admission webhook

constraints: PodSecurityPolicy has no drop-in replacement: the admission controller was removed together with the API, so the policy must be re-expressed.
Decide the intended Pod Security Standard (privileged, baseline, or restricted) for each namespace the policy covered before changing anything.
Remove Roles and ClusterRoles that grant `use` on the PodSecurityPolicy once it is gone.

steps.title: Choose a replacement policy
steps.instructions: Replace the PodSecurityPolicy with Pod Security Admission labels on the affected namespaces, or with a third-party admission webhook, as the Kubernetes migration guide describes.

steps.title: Remove references to the policy
steps.instructions: Delete the PodSecurityPolicy manifest and any Role or ClusterRole rule that grants `use` on it.

verification.purpose: Preview which existing pods would violate the chosen Pod Security Standard, without changing any namespace.
Validate the remaining manifests against the target Kubernetes version.

rules.title: Helm stable chart repository is end of life
rules.summary: The Helm project retired the stable chart repository: on 2020-11-13 CI was disabled and no further pull requests were accepted, and downloads were redirected to a read-only archive that receives no bug fixes or security patches. The Helm Chart Repository Deprecation Update states those dates and recommended actions.
rules.replacement: The chart's new maintained repository (see Helm's stable-repo-charts-new-locations list), or adopt the chart yourself

sources.title: Helm community: stable repository charts — new locations

constraints: Replace only Chart.yaml dependencies whose repository is the retired stable URL (https://charts.helm.sh/stable or https://kubernetes-charts.storage.googleapis.com).
Look up the chart name in Helm's stable-repo-charts-new-locations list for the maintainer's new repository; if none exists, consider adopting the chart rather than pinning the archive.

steps.title: Point the dependency at a maintained repository
steps.instructions: Change the reported dependency's repository URL to the chart's new location from the relocation list (or another maintainer-published repository), and set version to a release published there.

steps.title: Align other Chart.yaml dependencies
steps.instructions: Update every other Chart.yaml dependency that still names the retired stable repository URL.

verification.purpose: Fetch the dependency from the new repository and refresh Chart.lock.
Render the chart and validate the output against Kubernetes schemas.
